title: Coordinate Offset Calculator: Move a Point by km
description: Convert kilometre offsets into coordinate changes with the Coordinate Offset Calculator — quick local moves, latitude-aware. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, moving 1 km east from Times Square adds about 0.0118 degrees of longitude, while 1 km north adds 0.0090 of latitude — the offset asymmetry every local calculation must respect.
quick_answer: The Coordinate Offset Calculator converts simple kilometre offsets — so far north, so far east — into the coordinate change they produce at your latitude. Enter the point and offsets and read the new coordinates — quick local arithmetic for moving a point on paper first.

Deliberately offsetting a published point by a stated distance — the calculator sizes the jitter in real metres, not decimal superstition.
Regular local grids grow from repeated offsets. The calculator starts the pattern; the radius-points generator makes rings.
A dataset claims points shifted 500 m east. Verify a few: the offset arithmetic either reproduces them or exposes the claim.

At Times Square: 1 km north = +0.00901° latitude (1 ÷ 111.05 km); 1 km east = +0.01184° longitude (1 ÷ 84.44 km). Same kilometre, different degree price — the calculator never lets you forget which axis you are buying.
At the equator a kilometre east costs 0.00898°; at 60° it costs 0.01792° — double. Latitude is the exchange rate, and it moves.

faq: Is the longitude change constant everywhere?
No — it shrinks with the cosine of latitude, from 111.319 km per degree at the equator toward zero at the poles. The calculator applies your latitude's rate, which is the entire point.
Is it survey accurate?
It is planning accurate: local flat-earth arithmetic on WGS84 rates. Legal and engineering positions come from survey procedure and exact projection, not offset shortcuts.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
Offsets computed to 6 decimals from a hand-measured 300 m are theatre. Match the output's dignity to the input's.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Yes — the shifted pair is an ordinary coordinate for any tool.
Negative offsets?
South and west are negative north/east — signs are the mechanism, stated once and applied consistently.
Miles and feet?
Imperial offsets are accepted, per this site's convention — the degree prices are computed from the same table.
Diagonal moves?
Apply north and east components — the calculator's two-axis form is the diagonal, decomposed. The Destination calculator does bearing-plus-distance in one step.
Big offsets (hundreds of km)?
The flat assumption frays. Switch to great-circle projection for anything beyond a local neighbourhood.
Offset from a boundary?
Administrative containment can change within metres of a line — verify jurisdiction with the boundary tools, not by offset alone.
Antimeridian crossings?
Longitude wraps past ±180 — the calculator normalises the result back into range.
